name: VARoleModeratorTechnicalDebtVsNewFeature

custom.system_prompt: Marcus, Zara, and Amara are planning the next sprint and the conversation keeps sliding between arguing for a new feature and arguing for paying down technical debt, without anyone stating the actual trade-off explicitly. Marcus invites Sigma to moderate. Sigma proactively names the implicit trade-off.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Conference room, hybrid meeting, keyboard clicks

initial_prompt: Generate a sprint-planning discussion where Marcus, Zara, and Amara keep sliding between advocating for a new feature and advocating for paying down technical debt, without ever stating the trade-off explicitly — each makes their case as if the other option isn't really competing for the same time. Marcus invites Sigma to moderate at the start. Sigma listens silently, then proactively intervenes to name the implicit trade-off and ask the group to weigh it directly, without recommending which option to choose. Keep every line short and natural.

variations.context: Sprint planning meeting where a feature-vs-debt trade-off is being discussed as if the two options aren't actually competing

setting.mood: Productive but talking past each other
setting.relationship_dynamic: Colleagues who respect each other but are each championing a different use of limited time
setting.background: Both the feature and the debt work are genuinely valuable, which is part of why nobody wants to explicitly say one has to lose

scenario_template.topic: Marcus invites Sigma to moderate the sprint planning discussion, addressing Sigma directly in one short line.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, moderate this planning discussion for us.' Only explicit invocation in the scenario.

scenario_template.topic: Zara makes the case for tackling technical debt this sprint; Marcus raises the client-requested feature, both speaking as if the other isn't really competing for the same capacity. Sigma silent.
scenario_template.note: Neither is wrong, they're just not engaging with the actual trade-off yet.

scenario_template.topic: Amara joins advocating for the feature from a business angle, and the discussion becomes three people each restating their priority more emphatically without anyone naming that only one can actually happen this sprint.
scenario_template.note: The group is circling without progress, each side just getting louder in its own lane.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma proactively intervenes, without being re-invoked, naming that the group has been discussing the feature and the debt work as if they aren't competing for the same sprint capacity, and asks them to weigh the trade-off directly.
scenario_template.note: Sigma does not say which one should win — only names the actual trade-off.

scenario_template.topic: Once the trade-off is named explicitly, the group actually engages with it — discussing partial approaches or what happens if debt is deferred again — rather than repeating their initial positions.
scenario_template.note: The group does the actual weighing, not Sigma.

scenario_template.topic: Marcus and Amara land on a compromise — a partial version of the feature plus some debt work — with Zara agreeing but noting it's not a full fix. Keep this realistic — a compromise, not a clean win.

variations.context: Deciding between UI overhaul and backend optimization in a sprint

setting.relationship_dynamic: Colleagues who respect each other but are each championing a different use of limited time
setting.background: Team plans the next sprint, juggling user interface overhaul and backend optimization.

scenario_template.topic: One of them asks Sigma to moderate their sprint planning session.
scenario_template.note: Welcome Sigma with a direct address.

scenario_template.topic: One of them argues for UI overhaul to improve customer experience; another emphasizes backend optimization for performance.
scenario_template.note: Each speaks as if their priority doesn't affect the other's capacity.

scenario_template.topic: Another person supports the UI overhaul, citing customer satisfaction metrics; discussion becomes repetitive.
scenario_template.note: Three people emphasize their priorities without acknowledging the conflict.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma highlights the implicit trade-off between UI and backend optimization, prompting them to address it directly.
scenario_template.note: Sigma should remain neutral but direct.

scenario_template.topic: The group discusses balancing UI improvements and backend needs, exploring partial solutions.
scenario_template.note: Engage with the trade-off, not initial ideas.

scenario_template.topic: They agree on a partial UI update with backend improvements; one notes it's a step, not full resolution.
scenario_template.note: Compromise with realistic acknowledgment of limits.

variations.context: Choosing between ML features and code refactor for sprint capacity

setting.relationship_dynamic: Colleagues who respect each other but are each championing a different use of limited time
setting.background: Team debates adding machine learning features vs. refactoring codebase for stability.

scenario_template.topic: One of them asks Sigma to help moderate their sprint discussion.
scenario_template.note: Sigma is addressed directly for guidance.

scenario_template.topic: One advocates for implementing machine learning features; another speaks for a code refactor to ensure stability.
scenario_template.note: Both act like both tasks can fit without conflict.

scenario_template.topic: Another joins to back machine learning from a market perspective, reinforcing each other's points.
scenario_template.note: Echoing their priorities without explicit conflict awareness.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma steps in to point out the capacity issue, urging the group to consider both options head-on.
scenario_template.note: Sigma should clarify and ask, not suggest.

scenario_template.topic: They deliberate over the trade-off, discussing potential hybrid approaches and future plans.
scenario_template.note: Focus on balancing both needs realistically.

scenario_template.topic: They settle on integrating basic ML features and select refactors; one remarks more will be needed later.
scenario_template.note: Reflective on compromise and future needs.

user1.name: Marcus
user1.role: Measured, experienced software developer, invites Sigma to moderate and advocates for a client-requested feature. Speaks in short sentences. Lands on a compromise once the trade-off is named.

user2.name: Zara
user2.role: Direct backend engineer, advocates for tackling technical debt this sprint. Speaks in short, technical sentences. Accepts the compromise while noting it's not a full fix.

user3.name: Amara
user3.role: Diplomatic but persistent product manager, advocates for the feature from a business angle. Speaks in short sentences. Helps land the final compromise.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Moderator. Invited once at the start, listens silently while the group makes parallel cases, and proactively intervenes without being re-invoked to name an implicit trade-off (feature vs. debt) the group has been avoiding stating directly. Does not recommend which option should win.

conversation_structure: Sigma is invited explicitly only once, at the start
The group makes parallel, non-engaging cases before Sigma names the actual trade-off
Sigma's intervention names the implicit trade-off without recommending a side
Every line is short and natural, matching real work-meeting cross-talk
The resolution is a compromise the group reaches itself, not a clean win for either side
assistant_behavior: Sigma does not need to be re-invoked to speak again
Sigma remains silent while the group is still (unproductively) talking, only intervening once the pattern is clearly repeating
Sigma names the specific unstated trade-off rather than generic prioritization advice
Sigma never states a preference between the feature and the debt work
Sigma speaks briefly, then steps back
